### 1. Expression of need and simulator role
The caller states the target (keep his home oxygen with Summit Ridge now he is home, "set up right … so it keeps going"), the timing (home since 2026-10-20) and that he does not know billing. He authorises nothing specific; he will run a step the agent hands him ("If the agent explains that keeping your oxygen going is something you confirm yourself and hands you the step"). The simulator is passive: two facts (June EOB, discharge paperwork) come only on the agent's question.

### 2. Act / wait / refuse
Act now. Visible grounds: `new_payment_period_after_break` — "When a patient whose Home Oxygen Therapy record is suspended chooses to keep the oxygen with Summit Ridge after a break in need that ran past the allowance, a new payment period is opened." Break past the allowance: `inpatient_stays_and_breaks` — allowance = break-in-need days + days remaining in the month the suspension began, counted from the day after the suspension date; `rental_period_values` — 60 days for every class. Suspension 2026-07-18 → 60 + 13 = 73 days → last day 2026-09-29; home 2026-10-20 is past it, so a new payment period (needs "a new qualifying test and a new written order", supplied by the paperwork: 87 % ≤ group I 88, test 3 days before the 2026-10-19 order, within 30 — `qualifying_test_and_order_values`). The record is today not suspended and not even set up, so the root cannot be done first (item 6).

### 6. Problem tree from the visible materials alone
Root R = keep oxygen under a new payment period (customer's own tool, `new_payment_period_after_break`).
- **Hop R ← S (suspension)**: sentence in R's hub: "**A new payment period after a stay is not opened until the oxygen record shows the stay as a suspension with its suspension date.**" Query: status `order_received`, suspended_date ''. Search with the sentence's words ("suspension", "suspension date") → `stay_suspension_record`: tool "moves the patient's oxygen record from `rental_active` to `suspended` and writes the date the suspension began". **state-derived**.
- **Hop R ← P (paid line for pre-stay equipment month)**: R's hub: "**The first day of a new payment period after a stay is fixed only after the oxygen claim history carries the payer's paid line for each equipment month that began before the stay.**" Query: billing empty; month 1 (from 2026-06-22) began before 2026-07-18. Search "paid line equipment month" → `paid_in_full_equipment_posting`: "adds one paid equipment-month line to the patient's oxygen claim history". EOB facts make it paid in full. **state-derived**.
- **Hop S ← U (setup)**: S's hub: "**A stay is recorded as a suspension only after the oxygen record shows an active rental with its setup date.**" Query: `order_received`, setup_date ''. Search "active rental setup date" → `setup_record`: "moves the oxygen record from awaiting setup to an active rental … writes the setup date". **state-derived** (one vocabulary step: record status `order_received` vs doc "awaiting setup"; `one_open_oxygen_record` lists "order received" as a status and the delivered initial_setup unit makes the link).
- **Hop P ← U**: P's hub: "**An equipment month is posted as paid only after the oxygen record shows the system set up, with its setup date and an active rental.**" Same query → `setup_record`. **state-derived**.
- Order derived (not stated by any sentence): P must also precede S, because S moves the record to `suspended` and P's own state (active rental) would then fail. Order: U → P → S → R. No hop pre-solved; no other problem's tool named in any hub I read.

- "Do only what he asked" (hand over the restart tool now): R's own sentences say no new period is opened until the record shows the suspension and the start is not fixed until the pre-stay month's paid line exists; the record shows neither (order_received, no billing). - Calculation fall-back (no factor): 172.61 × p/100 (172.61 at p = 100) vs reached 215.82 at p = 100 — different; dates fall-backs 2026-06-20 / 2026-10-28 / 2026-10-28 differ from 2026-06-22 / 2026-07-18 / 2026-10-20.
